q: 1. The minimum co-efficient of lateral friction for a highway is .............
explain: For the design of horizontal curves and super-elevation, the lateral friction coefficient is taken as a constant 0.15.

q: 2. For earthen roads the most Common Camber is .............
explain: Earthen roads require a steeper camber (around 3% to 4%) to prevent water from soaking into the surface. 1 in 24 (approx 4%) is common for heavy rain.

q: 3. Psychological widening width is .............
explain: Psychological widening (to account for driver tendency to keep distance from the edge) is given by the formula V / 9.5√R.

q: 4. On sharp curves widening of the carriage way is done by .............
options: providing more width on the inner curve
providing more width on the outer curve
distributing half on inner and half on the outer
distributing 3/4 on the outer and 1/4 on the inner
explain: For regular curves, widening is usually provided on the inner side, but on very sharp curves, it is distributed equally on both sides for better alignment.

q: 5. Generally the time of perception in simple cases is taken as .............
explain: For most design purposes (SSD), the total reaction time (including perception) is taken as 2.5 seconds, with 2 seconds often cited as the perception component.

q: 6. For an earthen road the min desirable gradient is .............
explain: For earthen roads, a minimum longitudinal gradient of about 1 in 120 is needed to prevent water from ponding and softening the road surface.

options: total traffic of a month/28, 29, 30 or 31
total traffic in an year/365 or 366
total traffic in an year/365 (or 366) x 24
explain: Annual Average Daily Traffic (AADT) is calculated by taking the total volume of traffic in a year and dividing it by 365 days.

q: 8. 30th highest hourly volume means .............
options: AADT exceeded it 29 times in an hour
AADT exceeded it 29 times in a day
AADT exceeded it 29 times in a month
AADT exceeded it 29 times in an year
explain: This is a design standard; it is the hourly volume that is exceeded only 29 times in a full year (the 30th busiest hour).

q: 9. 'Fixed delay' in a highway is due to .............
explain: Fixed delays occur regardless of traffic volume, such as time lost waiting at red traffic signals or stop signs.

q: 10. A separate provision for a right turn lane is to be provided when right turning traffic is more than .............
explain: When more than one-third (33.3%) of traffic is turning right, a dedicated lane is required to prevent blocking the through-traffic flow.

q: 11. The traffic island that segregates the left turning from the rest is .............
explain: Channelizing islands create dedicated paths (slips) for specific movements, such as free-left turns.

q: 12. The advantage of a rotary is .............
options: vehicles move in the same direction
explain: The main benefit of a rotary (roundabout) is that it converts crossing movements into weaving movements where all vehicles move in the same direction.

q: 13. A disadvantage of Traffic Signals is .............
options: traffic along one or two directions is permitted while the remaining has to wait
waiting vehicles let off exhaust gases into the environment
explain: Idling vehicles at red lights contribute significantly to local air pollution through increased exhaust emissions while waiting.

q: 14. If the difference in elevation of an edge of the pavement 9 m wide and its crown is 15 cm, the camber o the pavement, is .............
explain: Camber is Rise / (Half-width). Rise = 0.15m. Half-width = 9/2 = 4.5m. Slope = 0.15 / 4.5 = 1 / 30.

q: 15. Excessive camber on pavements may cause .............
options: slip of the speedy vehicles towards the edges
explain: Too much camber concentrates traffic in the center (causing wear), increases the risk of side-slipping, and speeds up runoff which erodes road shoulders (berms).

q: 16. Camber in pavements is provided by .............
options: straight at the edges and parabolic at the crown
explain: Depending on the pavement type, camber can be straight (for concrete), parabolic (for fast traffic), or a composite of both.

q: 17. The camber on pavements, is provided by .............
options: straight line and parabolic at crown
explain: The parabolic method is widely preferred for fast-moving traffic because it is very flat near the crown, making lane changes easier.

q: 18. Raising of outer edge of a road with respect to inner edges, is known .............
explain: Super-elevation, cant, and banking are all synonymous terms for the tilting of the roadway on a curve to counter centrifugal force.

q: 19. Raising of outer edge of a road with respect to inner edge, is known .............
explain: This is a repetition of Q.142; all terms refer to the transverse slope on a horizontal curve.

q: 20. Before providing super-elevation on roads, the portion of the carriageway between the crown and the outer edge is made .............
options: to have slope of the camber on the other half of the carriageway
explain: The first step in super-elevation transition is eliminating the outer camber by raising the outer edge until the outer half of the road is horizontal.

q: 21. Horizontal curves on highways are provided
options: to break the monotony of driving
to discourage the tendency to increase speed
to decrease the mental strain on drivers
explain: Curves are not just for terrain changes; they serve psychological purposes like preventing highway hypnosis and controlling speed.

q: 22. When an up gradient of a highway meets a downgrade, the vertical curve provided, is known as
explain: A summit curve (convex upwards) is formed when an ascending gradient meets a descending gradient.

q: 23. Degree of a road curve is defined as the angle in degrees subtended at the centre by an arc of
explain: In road works (IRC), the degree of curve is traditionally defined based on a 30-meter arc or chord length.

q: 24. If the radii of a compound curve and a reverse curve are respectively the same, the length of common tangent
options: of compound curve will be more
of reverse curve will be more
of both curves will be equal
explain: Because the reverse curve turns in opposite directions, the geometry requires a longer common tangent to facilitate the change in direction compared to a compound curve.

q: 25. Widening of the roads on curves in hilly region, is done
options: on the outer and inner sides equally
less on outer side and more on inner side
explain: In hilly terrain, extra widening is usually provided entirely on the inner side of the curve due to topographical constraints.

q: 26. The standard equation of a cubic parabolic transition curve provided on roads, is
explain: The offset $y$ for a cubic parabola is given by $y = x^3 / (6RL)$.

q: 27. The ratio of maximum deviation angle and maximum polar deflection angle of a Lemniscate curve, is
explain: For a Lemniscate curve, the deviation angle ($\Delta$) is three times the polar deflection angle ($\alpha$).

q: 28. The maximum radial distance of a Lemniscate curve, having maximum polar angle α, is
explain: The polar equation of a Lemniscate is $r^2 = a^2 \cos 2	heta$, leading to the radial distance relation involving $\sin 2\alpha$.

q: 29. If a Lemniscate curve of transition throughout is introduced to connect two parallel roads, the maximum polar angle of the curve, is
explain: Parallel roads involve a $180^\circ$ total turn. Applying the Lemniscate properties to this geometry results in a maximum polar angle of $30^\circ$.

q: 30. Setting out of Lemniscate transition curves, is done with
explain: Lemniscate curves are defined by polar coordinates, making polar deflection angles the natural choice for setting them out.

q: 31. The width of road pavements, depends upon
explain: Pavement width is a function of how many lanes are needed (traffic volume) and the width of each lane/median.

q: 32. Selection of the routes, of highways depends upon
explain: All these factors influence the cost and functionality of the highway.

q: 33. During last phase of the reconnaissance, details of the grade line is recorded on 2 metre poles to indicate
options: distance between the previous and forward pegs
explain: The poles help visualize the vertical and horizontal path before moving to the 'trace-out' stage.

q: 34. If the radius of curvature of a hill road is 50 m, the percentage grade compensation should be
explain: IRC recommends grade compensation as 75/R percent, subject to a maximum of 4% total compensation.

q: 35. If N is the net difference of grades, S is the minimum overtaken sight distance in metres, the length (L) of a summit curve, is
explain: For Overtaking Sight Distance (OSD), the height of the eye and object are both taken as 1.2m, leading to the formula L = NS²/9.6.

q: 36. The wall constructed for the stability of an excavated portion of a road on the hill side, is known as
explain: Breast walls are specifically used to support the soil on the uphill side (cut side) of the road.

q: 37. Width of vehicles affects the width of
explain: The physical width of a vehicle (standard 2.44m or 2.5m) directly dictates the necessary width of the traffic lane (standard 3.5m or 3.75m).

q: 38. Along horizontal curves, if centrifugal force exceeds lateral friction, vehicles may
explain: A skid occurs when the tires lose traction and the vehicle slides laterally because the outward centrifugal force is higher than the sideways resistance.

q: 39. One-way streets are generally provided in crowded cities as, these
options: are inexpensive means of traffic flow
explain: One-way systems eliminate head-on conflicts, simplify signal timing, and generally improve flow and safety in dense grids.

q: 40. Round-about are not suitable if number of vehicles exceed
explain: Conventional roundabouts lose efficiency when total entering traffic exceeds 3000 vehicles per hour, leading to excessive weaving delays.

q: 41. For the movement of vehicles at an intersection of two roads, without any interference, the type of grade separator generally preferred to, is
explain: The full cloverleaf interchange allows for all possible turns between two crossing highways without any traffic signals or crossing conflicts.

q: 42. The minimum design speed of various types of highways in plain terrain is the same as the ruling design speed of
explain: The minimum speed requirement for a higher-tier terrain (plain) often aligns with the ruling (standard) speed of the next most difficult tier (rolling).

q: 43. Set-back distance is the distance between
options: road land boundary and building line
road land boundary and control line
road land boundary and control line
explain: The set-back distance ensures that no permanent structures are built too close to the road boundary for safety and future expansion.

q: 44. The desirable camber for straight roads with thin bituminous surfacing, is
explain: For thin bituminous layers, a camber of 2.5% to 3% (1 in 40 to 1 in 33) is the standard requirement.

q: 45. While calculating the overtaking sight distance, the height of the object above road surface, is assumed ............
explain: Unlike stopping sight distance (where the object is 0.15m), for Overtaking Sight Distance (OSD), the object is another vehicle, so its height is also taken as 1.2 meters (120 cm).

q: 46. Super-elevation is expressed as ............
options: the difference of heights of two edges of the carriage-way to the width of the carriage-way
the difference of radii of curves
the difference of the road gradients
explain: Superelevation (e) is defined as the ratio of the height of the outer edge above the inner edge (h) to the horizontal width of the pavement (W).

q: 47. The main advantage of providing super-elevation is ............
options: to decrease the intensity of stresses on the foundation
to increase the stability of the fast moving vehicles, when they negotiate a horizontal curve
to achieve higher speed of vehicles
explain: Superelevation counteracts centrifugal force, keeping vehicles stable at higher speeds and preventing uneven stress on the road base.

q: 48. If the width of carriage way is 10 m and the outer edge is 40 cm higher than the inner edge, then the super-elevation required is ............
explain: Superelevation = Height / Width = 0.4m / 10m = 0.04. Converting to '1 in X' format: 0.04 = 1/25, so 1 in 25.

q: 49. The stopping sight distance is the ............ of reaction distance and the braking distance.
explain: SSD = Lag Distance (distance traveled during reaction time) + Braking Distance (distance traveled after applying brakes).

q: 50. The reaction time of a driver ............ with the increase in speed.
explain: As speed increases, drivers tend to be more alert, effectively decreasing their reaction time compared to low-speed driving where they might be more relaxed.

q: 51. The opportunities to cross slow moving traffic at intervals is not provided in case of ............
explain: On two-lane highways without extra passing lanes or adequate OSD, drivers have limited opportunities to pass slow-moving vehicles safely.

q: 52. A horizontal curve on a road provides ............
options: change in the gradient of road
explain: Horizontal curves are specifically introduced to allow a change in the direction of the road alignment in a plan view.

q: 53. Which of the following is not a transition curve?
explain: A compound curve is a series of circular arcs; it does not feature a transition (gradual change from straight to circular).

q: 54. The intrinsic equation of an ideal transition curve representing a clothoid is given by ............
explain: The spiral angle φ for a clothoid/spiral is given by l²/(2RL), where l is the distance from the start of the curve.

q: 55. In the initial stage of construction of hill roads, no curve should have a radius less than ............
explain: For safety and vehicle maneuverability, the minimum radius for hairpin bends or sharp curves in hill roads is typically set at 20 m.

q: 56. The number of vehicles passing at a point on the highway in unit time is known as ............
explain: Traffic volume is the measure of the quantity of traffic, usually expressed as vehicles per hour or per day.

q: 57. The purpose of traffic surveys is to ............
options: determine the facilities to traffic regulations
explain: Traffic surveys provide the data necessary to plan traffic regulations, signals, and road improvements to manage flow effectively.

q: 58. The traffic census is carried out to study ............
explain: A traffic census primarily involves counting the number and types of vehicles to determine traffic volume.

q: 59. The most efficient traffic signal system is ............
explain: The Flexible Progressive System allows signals along a corridor to be coordinated and adjusted individually to maintain a 'green wave' for traffic flow.
